learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact, do not repeat words, and use a joining word when it helps.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, no repitas palabras y usa una palabra de unión cuando ayude.
learn.model: Monarchs visit milkweed and lay their eggs on it.
learn.notice: Two short sentences became one. The word milkweed is not repeated, and no facts are lost.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines these two monarch sentences best?
items.text: Monarchs visit milkweed. Monarchs lay eggs on milkweed.

options.text: Monarchs visit milkweed and monarchs lay eggs on milkweed.
Monarchs visit milkweed lay eggs on it.
Monarchs visit milkweed and lay eggs on it.

items.why: This choice keeps both facts, joins them with and, and does not repeat words.
items.whyEs: Esta opción conserva los dos datos, los une con and y no repite palabras.

items.prompt: Which combined sentence keeps all the facts about the caterpillar?
items.text: The caterpillar is striped. The caterpillar is hungry. The caterpillar crawls up the stem.

options.text: The striped caterpillar crawls up the stem.
The hungry, striped caterpillar crawls up the stem.
The hungry caterpillar is striped and crawls.

items.why: Hungry, striped, and crawls up the stem all stay in this sentence. The others leave out a fact.
items.whyEs: Hungry, striped y crawls up the stem están todos en esta oración. Las otras dejan fuera un dato.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that combines these two monarch sentences.
items.text: Monarchs fly south for the winter. They cannot survive the cold.
parts: Monarchs fly south for the winter
items.model: Monarchs fly south for the winter because they cannot survive the cold.
items.why: Because shows the reason monarchs fly south. The combined sentence keeps both facts.
items.whyEs: Because muestra la razón por la que las monarcas vuelan al sur. La oración combinada conserva los dos datos.

items.prompt: Check every combined sentence that keeps all three facts.
items.text: Facts: Monarchs are orange. Monarchs have black lines. Monarchs migrate to Mexico.

options.text: Monarchs are orange and migrate to Mexico.
Orange monarchs with black lines migrate to Mexico.
Monarchs have black lines and migrate.
Monarchs are orange and have black lines, and they migrate to Mexico.
Monarchs with black lines are orange.

items.why: A good combination keeps orange, black lines, and migrating to Mexico. The others lose at least one fact.
items.whyEs: Una buena combinación conserva orange, black lines y migrating to Mexico. Las otras pierden al menos un dato.

items.prompt: Which joining word keeps the meaning of these two sentences about the trip south?
items.text: The nights grew cold. The monarchs began their trip.

options.text: The monarchs began their trip although the nights grew cold.
The monarchs began their trip when the nights grew cold.
The monarchs began their trip unless the nights grew cold.

items.why: When keeps the real order of events. Although and unless change what the sentences mean.
items.whyEs: When conserva el orden real de los sucesos. Although y unless cambian lo que significan las oraciones.

items.prompt: Which combined sentence about milkweed has no repeated words?
items.text: Milkweed is a plant. Milkweed has pink flowers. Milkweed grows in fields.

options.text: Milkweed is a plant, milkweed has pink flowers, and milkweed grows in fields.
Milkweed is a plant and milkweed has pink flowers in fields.
Milkweed is a plant with pink flowers that grows in fields.

items.why: Milkweed appears once, and all three facts are still there.
items.whyEs: Milkweed aparece una sola vez y los tres datos siguen estando.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: Ladybugs are red. Ladybugs have black spots. Ladybugs eat tiny insects called aphids.

label: I kept the facts about spots or aphids
Conservé los datos de las manchas o los áfidos

write.model: Red ladybugs with black spots eat tiny insects called aphids.

familyTalk.en: Pick two short facts about a pet and join them into one sentence with and.
familyTalk.es: Elijan dos datos cortos sobre una mascota y únanlos en una oración con and.

teacherTip.en: Write the short sentences on strips and let pairs physically move words to build one combined sentence.
teacherTip.es: Escribe las oraciones cortas en tiras y deja que las parejas muevan las palabras para armar una oración combinada.

learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact, do not repeat words, and use a joining word when it helps.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, no repitas palabras y usa una palabra de unión cuando ayude.
learn.model: Farmers dug canals that carried river water to their fields.
learn.notice: The word that joins two ideas. The word canals is not repeated.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines these two Mesopotamia sentences best?
items.text: Farmers dug canals. The canals carried river water to their fields.

options.text: Farmers dug canals the canals carried river water to their fields.
Farmers dug canals that carried river water to their fields.
Farmers dug canals, that carried, river water.

items.why: That joins the two ideas without repeating canals. The other choices are run-ons or break up the meaning.
items.whyEs: That une las dos ideas sin repetir canals. Las otras opciones son oraciones sin pausa (run-on) o rompen el significado.

items.prompt: Which joining word keeps the meaning of these flood sentences?
items.text: The rivers flooded. The soil became rich.

options.text: The rivers flooded because the soil became rich.
The rivers flooded but the soil became rich.
The rivers flooded, so the soil became rich.

items.why: The flood caused the rich soil, so so keeps the meaning. Because reverses the cause, and but adds a false contrast.
items.whyEs: La inundación causó el suelo fértil, así que so conserva el significado. Because invierte la causa y but agrega un contraste falso.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that combines these two scribe sentences.
items.text: Scribes pressed symbols into wet clay. The clay dried hard.
parts: Scribes pressed symbols into wet clay,
items.model: Scribes pressed symbols into wet clay, and the clay dried hard.
items.why: And adds the second fact to the first without changing the meaning.
items.whyEs: And agrega el segundo dato al primero sin cambiar el significado.

items.prompt: Check every combined sentence that keeps all three facts about Ur.
items.text: Facts: Ur was a city. Ur was in Mesopotamia. Ur had a tall temple.

options.text: Ur was a city with a tall temple.
Ur was a city in Mesopotamia with a tall temple.
Ur was in Mesopotamia and was a city.
Ur, a city in Mesopotamia, had a tall temple.
Ur was a tall temple in Mesopotamia.

items.why: A correct combination keeps city, Mesopotamia, and tall temple without changing the meaning.
items.whyEs: Una combinación correcta conserva city, Mesopotamia y tall temple sin cambiar el significado.

items.prompt: Which combined sentence about merchants has no repeated words?
items.text: Merchants lived in Ur. Merchants traded grain in Ur. Merchants traded wool in Ur.

options.text: Merchants lived in Ur and traded grain in Ur and wool in Ur.
Merchants lived in Ur, they traded grain, they traded wool.
Merchants who lived in Ur traded grain and wool.

items.why: Merchants and Ur each appear once, and grain and wool are joined with and.
items.whyEs: Merchants y Ur aparecen una vez, y grain y wool se unen con and.

items.prompt: Which joining word keeps the meaning of these two city sentences?
items.text: The city grew. Many people moved there for work.

options.text: The city grew although many people moved there for work.
The city grew because many people moved there for work.
The city grew unless many people moved there for work.

items.why: Because shows the reason the city grew. Although and unless do not fit the facts.
items.whyEs: Because muestra la razón por la que la ciudad creció. Although y unless no encajan con los datos.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: The Nile is long. It flows north. It ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

label: I kept the facts about north or the sea
Conservé los datos sobre el norte o el mar

write.model: The long Nile flows north and ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

familyTalk.en: Tell about your street with two short facts, then join them into one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten sobre su calle con dos datos cortos y luego únanlos en una sola oración.

teacherTip.en: Point out how combined sentences read more smoothly aloud; have students read the choppy version and the combined version.
teacherTip.es: Muestra que las oraciones combinadas suenan más fluidas al leerlas; pide que lean la versión entrecortada y la combinada.

learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact, do not repeat words, and use a joining word when it helps.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, no repitas palabras y usa una palabra de unión cuando ayude.
learn.model: A triangle has three sides and three angles.
learn.notice: Two short sentences became one. The word triangle is used once and both facts are kept.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines these two triangle sentences best?
items.text: A triangle has three sides. A triangle has three angles.

options.text: A triangle has three sides and a triangle has three angles.
A triangle has three sides and three angles.
A triangle has three sides three angles.

items.why: This choice joins the facts with and and does not repeat the words a triangle has.
items.whyEs: Esta opción une los datos con and y no repite las palabras a triangle has.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines these two square facts correctly?
items.text: A square is a rectangle. All of its sides are equal.

options.text: A square is a rectangle because all of its sides are equal.
A square is a rectangle but all of its sides are equal.
A square is a rectangle with four equal sides.

items.why: With keeps both facts. Because would give a wrong reason, and but would add a false contrast.
items.whyEs: With conserva los dos datos. Because daría una razón incorrecta y but agregaría un falso contraste.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that combines these two number sentences.
items.text: Ten is greater than seven. Ten is less than twelve.
items.model: Ten is greater than seven and less than twelve.
items.why: And joins the two facts about ten: it is greater than seven and less than twelve.
items.whyEs: And une los dos datos sobre el diez: es mayor que siete y menor que doce.

items.prompt: Check every combined sentence that keeps all the hexagon facts.
items.text: Facts: A hexagon has six sides. A hexagon is a polygon. Honeycomb cells are hexagons.

options.text: Honeycomb cells are polygons.
A hexagon is a polygon with six sides, and honeycomb cells are hexagons.
Hexagons are honeycomb cells with six sides.
Honeycomb cells are hexagons, polygons with six sides.

items.why: Good combinations keep six sides, polygon, and honeycomb cells. The others lose a fact or change its meaning.
items.whyEs: Las buenas combinaciones conservan six sides, polygon y honeycomb cells. Las otras pierden un dato o cambian su significado.

items.prompt: Which combined sentence about the rectangle has no repeated words?
items.text: The rectangle is long. The rectangle is narrow. The rectangle is blue.

options.text: The rectangle is long, the rectangle is narrow, the rectangle is blue.
The rectangle is long and the rectangle is narrow and the rectangle is blue.
The long, narrow rectangle is blue.

items.why: Rectangle appears once, and long, narrow, and blue all stay.
items.whyEs: Rectangle aparece una vez y long, narrow y blue se conservan.

items.prompt: Which joining word keeps the meaning of these two counting sentences?
items.text: I counted the tiles twice. I wanted to be sure my total was right.

options.text: I counted the tiles twice although I wanted to be sure my total was right.
I counted the tiles twice because I wanted to be sure my total was right.
I counted the tiles twice unless I wanted to be sure my total was right.

items.why: Because gives the reason for counting twice. The other joining words do not make sense.
items.whyEs: Because da la razón para contar dos veces. Las otras palabras de unión no tienen sentido.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: A cube has six faces. The faces are square. The faces are equal.

label: I kept the facts about faces
Conservé los datos sobre las caras

write.model: A cube is a solid shape with six equal square faces.

familyTalk.en: Look at a box at home. Say two short facts about it, then join them into one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Miren una caja en casa. Digan dos datos cortos sobre ella y únanlos en una oración.

teacherTip.en: After combining, have students check the new sentence against the originals and tick off each fact.
teacherTip.es: Después de combinar, pide que los estudiantes comparen la nueva oración con las originales y marquen cada dato.
